authoredSolutions.51: Both numerator and denominator vanish at \(x=0\), so use series. Since \(\tan x-x\sim\frac{x^3}{3}\), we get \(e^{\tan x-x}-1\sim\tan x-x\sim\frac{x^3}{3}\), and \(e^x\to1\), so the first part \(\to\frac{x^3}{3}\). Also \(\log_e(\sec x+\tan x)-x=\int_0^x(\sec u-1)\,du\sim\frac{x^3}{6}\). Numerator \(\sim\frac{x^3}{3}+\frac{x^3}{6}=\frac{x^3}{2}\) and denominator \(\sim\frac{x^3}{3}\). Hence \(f(0)=\dfrac{x^3/2}{x^3/3}=\frac{3}{2}\).
